title: Lifeline
author: Kafkapharnaum
rules:
After Renbans and German Whispers, here’s one more Still Life setting challenge, this time using just Region Sum Lines. Big thanks to wullemuus and chrisj50 for testing it.

This time, in the most unexpected and extreme case of absolute unlikelihood, I have actually learned something, and after Covalent Adduct was deemed to be nowhere near the 5/5 I had estimated, and this one here having been put at 3.5/5 by one of the tester, I am starting it at 4/5, despite thinking deep down that it’s still harder that the 4/5 rated Cambrian (the Renbans one). Anyway, as always, you can find here a complete list of all the Still Life puzzles, and Sktx's examples highlighting many of the common pitfalls further below.

Click on the puzzle to play

RULES

Normal sudoku rules apply

• Each of the digits 1 to 9 must appear once in every row, column and 3x3 box.

• The color indications below are but suggestions and do not affect anything.

STILL LIFE

• Shade some cells green ("active cells") such that the – up to – eight cells neighboring each green cell contain exactly 2 or 3 other green cells and the neighbors of each 'unshaded' – or black/red/blue/etc. – cell ("inactive cells") do not contain exactly 3 green cells.

REGION SUM LINES

• The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments of the same sums. The sums may differ from line to line.

— Every digit on a Region Sum Line must correctly indicate either the number of active cells or of inactive cells in its neighborhood – that is, its own cell and all orthogonally and diagonally adjacent cells.

==== EXAMPLES ====

Example 1

In Example 1, a 3x3 box with a Game of Life pattern is shown (green for active cells, grey for inactive cells).
But the cells marked with a ! are unstable : they either are inactive but with 3 active neighbors, or active but with less than 2 or more than 3 active neighbors. Therefore this pattern is not a Still Life pattern, and can not appear in a Still Life Sudoku puzzle.

Example 2

In Example 2 (using the digits of a normal 9x9 sudoku grid), a 3x3 box is shown filled with digits and clues (circles and squares), the Game of Life pattern that is shown is stable, and all the clues are fulfilled. This could appear in a Still Life Sudoku puzzle.
solutionCode: From top to bottom, the digits in the 'active' cells of column 3, followed by those of column 5
